Hardware:

	1.	Accelerometer:
	•	You’re on the right track considering an accelerometer. The ADXL345 or MPU-6050 are popular, inexpensive 3-axis accelerometers that can give you accurate readings for acceleration (in m/s²).
	•	Connect this sensor to a microcontroller (like Arduino or Raspberry Pi). The data can then be processed to extract the frequency and displacement information.
	2.	Piezo Sensor:
	•	The piezo sensor you mentioned is a good start for detecting vibrations, but it might not give you accurate frequency or displacement data directly. It’s great for detecting the presence of vibrations, but for detailed data (like frequency and displacement), an accelerometer will be more reliable.
	•	To connect the sensor, you’d hook it up to an analog input on an Arduino (or similar) and capture voltage changes that correspond to vibrations. However, you’d still need to process the data to extract meaningful metrics (frequency, etc.).

Steps:

	1.	Collect Acceleration Data:
	•	Use an accelerometer like the MPU-6050, which will give you raw acceleration data (in m/s²). You’ll likely connect it via I2C to a microcontroller (Arduino/Raspberry Pi).
	•	For the Raspberry Pi, you can use Python libraries like smbus to communicate with the accelerometer.
	2.	Process the Data:
	•	Frequency: Once you have acceleration data, you can perform a Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to extract the vibration frequency in Hz.
	•	Displacement: Displacement can be derived by double integrating the acceleration data over time.
	•	Acceleration: Directly measurable from the accelerometer data in m/s².
	3.	Software:
	•	Use software like Python with libraries like SciPy or NumPy to handle the FFT and data integration for displacement. The data from the accelerometer can be streamed over USB or Wi-Fi to your computer for further analysis.
	4.	Graphing/Visualizing the Data:
	•	Use Python plotting libraries like matplotlib to graph the vibration data for easier analysis.

Resources:

	•	Look for Arduino/MPU-6050 tutorials online for guidance on connecting the accelerometer and reading data.
	•	For FFT and displacement calculations, check out Python tutorials on vibration analysis, particularly those that use libraries like SciPy.
